newsitem.title: UK: Long-haul dirty tankers perk up after lull.
newsitem.headline: Long-haul dirty tankers perk up after lull.

text.p: Long-haul dirty tanker rates showed signs of strength on Tuesday after a lacklustre couple of weeks, boosted by heavy demand and a lack of ships in several sectors, brokers said.
One-million-barrel West Africa/U.S. cargoes edged up to W95/97.5 in active trade, with one broker saying, "We could see West Africa up to W100 next week if things continue as they are."
He put very large crude carriers (VLCCs) on this route at a firm W65/67.5, and added that the key Middle East sector was also perking up.
Mideast/Japan VLCCs firmed to W65/67.5 after falling to W57.5 last week when brokers were sidelined by IP Week, while to the west they edged up to W52.5 from W50.
The Lyria was fixed at W55 to Singapore for Exxon, up five points, while Saudi Arabia's Vela fixed two vessels to the U.S. Gulf at W49.5 with options to the Red Sea at W52.5.
The transatlantic market was quiet, with no VLCCs seen fixed but brokers said the notional rate remained at W65, in line with West Africa, while 130,000 tonners were flat at about W92.5.
The cross-Med and inter-U.K./Cont markets were also stable, with 80,000 tonne cargoes at W110.
Fuel oil was also steady to slightly firmer with tonnage and requirements broadly in balance, brokers said. Inter-U.K./Cont 20,000 tonne cargoes were fixed at W205, with cross-Med at W200.

The Caribbean sector slipped after 70,000 tonne cargoes surged on Monday to W150 from W120. Brokers said this sector had dipped to W142.5, while 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes edged up to W185/190 from W185.
